message.content: Every few hours the daemon stalls for seconds at a time. The disk shows a multi-gigabyte db.sqlite-wal file right before each stall.

WAL mode appends every write to the write-ahead log and only folds it back into the main database on checkpoint. With autocheckpoint disabled the WAL grows unbounded, and the eventual checkpoint rewrites gigabytes while holding the write lock — that is your stall.
So checkpoint more aggressively. What did you land on?
Set wal_autocheckpoint to 1000 pages and run an explicit PASSIVE checkpoint when the daemon goes idle. The WAL stays under a few megabytes and the stalls are gone.
